A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AllTracker study. The text, equations, seven figures, ten tables, and appendices A–F are readable and matchable despite bibliography and appendix reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original AllTracker benchmark evaluations, architecture and training ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary SINTEL/CVO results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the point-tracking comparisons, ablations, and supplementary optical-flow evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same encoder, correlation pyramids, spatial/temporal refinement blocks, losses, upsampling, and sliding-window inference. The new precision disclosure does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same optical-flow and point-tracking training datasets, nine point-tracking benchmarks, and SINTEL/CVO evaluations. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the tables and qualitative comparisons, including the CoTracker variants, DELTA, and AccFlow/DOT in CVO. TAPNext is newly cited but is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, resolutions, metrics, video-length restrictions, query selection, and baseline evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B newly documents bfloat16 usage without reporting a switch from an earlier precision setting.

E4.justification: The temporal-module, motion-representation, backbone, hyperparameter, loss, and frame-shuffling ablations are unchanged. The baseline-protocol comparison, refinement-iteration analysis, and qualitative case studies are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. Table 1 retains average accuracy of 66.1 for AllTracker versus 65.0 for CoTracker3; Table 2 retains 69.5 versus 66.9 at 768 × 1024. Appendix optical-flow scores and plotted trends are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss expressions, coordinate updates, and accuracy metric remain equivalent, including Equations (1)–(2). Neither version introduces additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The claims about efficient, dense, high-resolution tracking and joint training remain unchanged. The revised abstract explicitly names optical-flow and point-tracking datasets, a contribution already stated in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: The spatial-coherence interpretation, baseline query-bias discussion, optical-flow underfitting explanation, and compute/window-size limitations are retained. The added citation supports an existing future-work suggestion without changing its meaning.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly states that training uses mixed precision in PyTorch with bfloat16. This adds useful implementation information absent from v1; the other implementation details and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds TAPNext as reference [60] to the conclusion's existing suggestion about more expressive models. Other reference renumberings and preprint-to-publication updates concern retained works and do not substantially change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the abstract's dataset wording, makes small grammar and terminology edits, standardizes bibliographic entries, and moves an introductory sentence within Appendix F. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds gray highlighting to the average columns in Tables 1–4 and 8. Bibliography compression and appendix reflow relocate Figure 6 and Table 9 and give the supplement a clean page opening; figure content, axes, captions, and table membership remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 fills a small reproducibility gap by specifying PyTorch bfloat16 training in Appendix B. Clearer abstract wording, bibliographic corrections, and highlighted table averages also modestly improve usability. The scientific evidence and limitations are preserved, so the overall improvement is limited.
